name: hotel
description: Rooms and room types, reservations and availability, seasonal rates, cancellation fees and invoices for a small hotel.
author: test2 benchmark author

issues.anchor: return self.check_in <= check_out and check_in <= self.check_out
issues.description: Stays are half-open (the guest leaves on the check-out day), but the inclusive comparisons make back-to-back stays overlap, so a room cannot be booked from the day the previous guest leaves.
issues.fix_hint: Use strict comparisons: self.check_in < check_out and check_in < self.check_out.

issues.description: The default list is shared by every reservation made without explicit requests, so add_request on one reservation shows up on all the others.
issues.fix_hint: Default to None and store a fresh list (list(special_requests or [])).

issues.description: The docstring says VAT is charged on the whole subtotal, room and extras, but it is computed on the room charge only.
issues.fix_hint: Compute VAT on subtotal instead of room_charge.

issues.description: The file name comes from the front desk (the guest's receipt) and is joined to the archive root unchecked, so '../' names read any file the process can read.
issues.fix_hint: Resolve the path and refuse names that do not resolve to a file directly inside the archive root.

issues.description: reservations imports cancellation to price a cancellation, and cancellation imports reservations back for the Reservation type and Status enum; the policy should depend only on plain data or the dependency should go one way.
Six levels of nested for/if to decide whether a room is taken; the inner loop over every reservation per room could be one any() over a helper (or the book's is_available).
Private helper that nothing calls (and duplicates the average-night formula of the cancellation policy).

decoys.why_it_is_fine: It iterates over a copy of the list, so removing from the original while looping is safe.
The broad except only logs which record failed and re-raises the original error, as the docstring promises.
